workload.problem: damped harmonic oscillator x'' + 2 zeta omega x' + omega^2 x = 0, classical RK4, fixed step (perf_card.py)

arm_labels.eagle_term8: eagle host, termination loop, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_compact8: eagle host, termination + compaction, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder8: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder1: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, 1 thread

arms.eagle_term8: The GPU card's eagle graph arm, unchanged, on the host: the same hawk step kernel, eagle.deploy and eagle.until_done call, run by eagle's OpenMP host team; one code base for GPUs and CPUs. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 41.3 ms; spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 400 ms; uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 693 ms. Fastest in 3 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_term1: The same loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 321 ms (7.78× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.16 s (7.9× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 5.52 s (7.96× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact8: The GPU card's compaction arm on the host: the launch covers only the samples still running, the map rebuilt every 16 steps when a sample finished. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 64.5 ms (1.56× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 419 ms (1.05× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.1 s (1.59× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact1: The compaction loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 182 ms (4.4× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.27 s (3.16× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 4.58 s (6.61× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder8: The GPU card's reorder arm on the host: the live samples moved to the front of every plane when they spread thin, restored to sample order at the end (inside the wall). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 164 ms (3.97× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 470 ms (1.17× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.08 s (1.56× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder1: The reorder loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 251 ms (6.07× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.23 s (3.08× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 4.58 s (6.61× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numba_prange: Compiles a plain Python loop to machine code with no separate language; each sample keeps its state in registers across all of its steps and stops on its own, so finished samples cost nothing. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 39.9 ms (0.967× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 398 ms (0.995× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.85 s (2.67× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 8 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_shard8: The JAX arm spread over 8 CPU devices: the batch is sharded and each shard runs its own vmapped while loop, with no cross-shard step synchronisation. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 217 ms (5.25× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.15 s (5.36× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.14 s (3.09× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 1 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_vmap: Compiles the whole loop once and batches a per-sample while loop with vmap; the same code runs on GPUs and differentiates with jax.grad. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 360 ms (8.72× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.42 s (8.55× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.47 s (5.01× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.torch_masked: Runs the masked array version on a multi-threaded tensor library; it fits where the computation already lives next to a PyTorch model or needs autograd. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 870 ms (21.1× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 8.19 s (20.5× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 8.37 s (12.1× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numpy_masked: No compile step and no dependency beyond NumPy; masked array code computes every sample every step, so it fits dense batches where all samples run to the end (the uniform configuration). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 2.2 s (53.3× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 21.6 s (54.1× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 19.6 s (28.3× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.mp_numpy: Spreads NumPy over processes with the standard library alone; each chunk stops once its own samples are done. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 494 ms (12× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 4.07 s (10.2× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 4.04 s (5.83× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.python_loops: Nothing to install and each line can be stepped in a debugger; run only at small N here. On this card: spread S=100, N=10,000: 66.4 ms (142× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=10,000: 632 ms (148× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000: 289 ms (379× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
